_readme: Supported games: how to find them and the settings card shown for each. Card items: 'do' = the setting, 'why' = the reason, optional 'only' = nvidia | amd. Keep every line backed by testing or the developer; put unproven ideas under 'Try and measure'.

items.why: Most consistent frame pacing and the lowest input delay.
Gameplay runs at 60. Going higher changes nothing in the fight and only adds load spikes.
VSync adds input delay. Cap with the in-game limit (or RTSS) instead.

items.do: Upscaling: native, DLSS or NIS. Avoid FSR 2
items.why: FSR 2 adds noticeable input lag in this game.

items.do: Shadows and post-processing Low, motion blur and film grain Off
items.why: Headroom is what keeps 60 locked during supers and stage transitions.

card.section: NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > Program settings > TEKKEN 8

items.why: Keeps the GPU render queue short, which matters most when the GPU is the bottleneck.

items.do: Power management mode: Prefer maximum performance
items.why: Stops the GPU from downclocking between frames at a light 60 FPS load.

items.do: Leverless / arcade stick: plug it into a rear motherboard USB port, not a hub or the front panel
items.why: Direct ports avoid shared-hub polling hiccups. SteadyFrame already disables USB selective suspend so the port never sleeps.

items.do: Keyboard players: check the Steam overlay frame-time graph while walking
items.why: The built-in keyboard support causes frame-time spikes on movement inputs. The fix is making it show up as a controller (a leverless or HID-Remapper).
Shaders compile during the first matches; early stutter after an update is expected.

items.do: Optional: RTSS frame limit 60 instead of the in-game limit
items.why: RivaTuner's limiter gives the most even frame pacing. Use one limiter, not both.
No measured gain, the game can overwrite them, and Bandai Namco does ban accounts for modified clients.
Most consistent frame pacing and latency.

items.do: Limit FPS Always: On, a bit above your refresh rate or at a level your PC holds steadily
items.why: A rate the PC can always hit gives steadier frame times than an uncapped number that bounces around.

items.do: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency: On + Boost
items.why: Syncs CPU and GPU so frames don't queue up; lowers system latency.

card.section: In game: Settings > Video > Graphics Quality

items.why: Spreads render work across cores; better lows on modern CPUs.

items.do: Material, Texture, Detail: Low or Medium. VSync Off. Vignette, Bloom, Distortion, Cast Shadows Off
items.why: Less GPU load spikes in fights, cleaner image for spotting.

items.do: Raw Input Buffer: nothing to do
items.why: Riot made it permanent in patch 11.06; the toggle is gone.

items.do: Keep TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on
items.why: Vanguard needs them on Windows 11. SteadyFrame never touches VBS/HVCI either.
Riot syncs settings from the cloud and overwrites the file.
Most consistent frame pacing and latency.

items.do: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency: Enabled + Boost
items.why: Cuts the render queue; lower latency without costing FPS.

items.do: Cap fps_max instead of running unlimited (around what your PC holds in a busy deathmatch; 400 is a common tested value)
items.why: In community testing a 400 cap gave far better 1% lows than unlimited, at a slightly lower average.
Adds input delay. Use the fps cap (and G-Sync/FreeSync if you have it).
Visibility; the cost is small.

items.do: +exec autoexec (only if you use an autoexec)
items.why: Makes sure the autoexec loads; guides disagree on whether CS2 always runs it by itself.

items.do: -allow_third_party_software only if you need OBS game capture
items.why: It may affect Trust Factor.
Windows already favors the foreground game; forcing High can add input lag.
The engine detects cores itself; forcing it can cause stutter.
Refresh is auto-detected, 0 is already the default, -novid only skips the intro.
Tested: +8% average FPS but 15% worse 1% lows. Only keep it if your own benchmark says so.
Community-reported frame pacing / latency improvement, not documented by Valve. Compare 1% lows with and without.
